dimensions.label: Competent, independent, impartial tribunal established by law
dimensions.standard: The adjudicating tribunal must be competent, independent, impartial and established by law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law.
dimensions.exceptions: An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.
questions: What law establishes the tribunal's authority?
What evidence addresses competence, interference, conflicts or objective appearance of bias?
dimensions.applicability: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law. An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.

dimensions.label: Equality before courts and equality of arms
dimensions.standard: Equality before courts and tribunals requires equal access and procedural opportunities; distinctions require objective, reasonable justification without actual disadvantage or unfairness.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law.
dimensions.exceptions: Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.
questions: Could the parties access the tribunal and make submissions?
Did disclosure, resources or procedure put one party at material disadvantage, with what justification?
dimensions.applicability: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law. Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.

dimensions.label: Public hearings and public judgments
dimensions.standard: Hearings and judgments must ordinarily be public; permitted exclusions and judgment exceptions require case-specific justification.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Hearing and judgment in determination of a criminal charge or suit at law; determine hearing type, as not every pretrial/appeal step requires a public hearing.
dimensions.exceptions: Press/public may be excluded for morals, public order, national security in a democratic society, private lives, or strictly necessary special circumstances where publicity prejudices justice. Judgment exceptions include juvenile interests or matrimonial/child guardianship disputes.
questions: Was the hearing open to the public, and were any exclusions justified?
Was the judgment made public, subject to applicable exceptions?
components: Exception justification; missing web copies are evidence gaps, not proof
dimensions.applicability: Hearing and judgment in determination of a criminal charge or suit at law; determine hearing type, as not every pretrial/appeal step requires a public hearing. Press/public may be excluded for morals, public order, national security in a democratic society, private lives, or strictly necessary special circumstances where publicity prejudices justice. Judgment exceptions include juvenile interests or matrimonial/child guardianship disputes.

dimensions.label: Presumption of innocence
dimensions.standard: Everyone charged with a criminal offence is presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law; the prosecution bears the burden and authorities must refrain from prejudging guilt.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through adjudication.
dimensions.exceptions: Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.
questions: Who bore the burden and what proof standard was used?
Did authorities prejudge guilt or present the accused as guilty?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through adjudication. Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.

dimensions.label: Notice of charges
dimensions.standard: Prompt, detailed notice in a language understood of the nature and cause of the criminal charge.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges.
dimensions.exceptions: Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.
questions: When did the person learn the charge and alleged acts?
What details and language were provided?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges. Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.

dimensions.label: Adequate time and facilities for defence
dimensions.standard: Adequate time and facilities to prepare the defence, including access to relevant documents and other evidence needed for defence.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps.
dimensions.exceptions: Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.
questions: What preparation time, case complexity and disclosure were available?
Were necessary adjournments/access requested and how were requests decided?
dimensions.applicability: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps. Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.

dimensions.label: Access to effective legal assistance
dimensions.standard: Defence in person or through legal assistance of choice, confidential access to counsel, and assigned effective assistance where justice requires subject to means conditions.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal defence; distinguish custodial/investigation guarantees under Article 9 and applicable domestic law.
dimensions.exceptions: Assigned assistance depends on interests of justice and lack of means for free assistance. Self-representation restrictions require objective sufficiently serious reasons; attributed counsel errors require case-specific responsibility analysis.
questions: Was counsel chosen/assigned, accessible and confidential?
Were required assistance and effective representation available, with what restrictions?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal defence; distinguish custodial/investigation guarantees under Article 9 and applicable domestic law. Assigned assistance depends on interests of justice and lack of means for free assistance. Self-representation restrictions require objective sufficiently serious reasons; attributed counsel errors require case-specific responsibility analysis.

dimensions.label: Presence and meaningful participation
dimensions.standard: An accused ordinarily has a right to be tried in their presence and meaningfully defend the case.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal trial and defence participation.
dimensions.exceptions: Proceedings in absence can be permissible in specific circumstances after sufficient notice and opportunity; verify steps informing the accused and justification, not absence alone.
questions: Was the accused present, informed and able to follow/respond?
If absent or restricted, what notice/opportunity and reasons existed?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal trial and defence participation. Proceedings in absence can be permissible in specific circumstances after sufficient notice and opportunity; verify steps informing the accused and justification, not absence alone.

dimensions.label: Examine witnesses and present defence evidence
dimensions.standard: Examine prosecution witnesses and obtain/examine defence witnesses under the same conditions; meaningful opportunity to challenge material evidence.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal trial and material defence evidence requests.
dimensions.exceptions: This is not an unlimited right to call every witness. Identify relevance, requests, refusals, reasons and disadvantage.
questions: Could material prosecution witnesses/evidence be challenged?
Could relevant defence witnesses/evidence be presented under comparable conditions?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal trial and material defence evidence requests. This is not an unlimited right to call every witness. Identify relevance, requests, refusals, reasons and disadvantage.

dimensions.label: Interpretation where required
dimensions.standard: Free assistance of an interpreter where the accused cannot understand or speak the language used in court.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken.
dimensions.exceptions: Nationality or multilingual setting alone does not prove need or adequacy. This right does not require proceedings in the preferred language where the court language is sufficiently understood.
questions: What language ability and proceedings language are documented?
Was free, adequate interpretation provided throughout relevant proceedings?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken. Nationality or multilingual setting alone does not prove need or adequacy. This right does not require proceedings in the preferred language where the court language is sufficiently understood.

dimensions.label: Protection against compelled self-incrimination
dimensions.standard: No compulsion to testify against oneself or confess guilt; exclude prohibited coercion and examine allegations of involuntary statements.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial.
dimensions.exceptions: Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.
questions: How was the statement obtained and was compulsion alleged?
How did the court handle coercion allegations and use/exclusion?
dimensions.applicability: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial. Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.

dimensions.label: Trial without undue delay
dimensions.standard: Criminal proceedings must proceed without undue delay, assessed from formal charge through final judgment including appeal.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal.
dimensions.exceptions: Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.
questions: What intervals, procedural steps and reasons for delay are documented?
How do complexity, party conduct, court conduct and detention affect adequacy?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal. Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.

dimensions.label: Review of conviction and sentence
dimensions.standard: Conviction and sentence must be reviewed by a higher tribunal according to law, including sufficient substantive review of facts and law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review.
dimensions.exceptions: Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.
questions: Was higher review available and effective for both conviction and sentence?
What facts/law, judgment and record were reviewed and what barriers existed?
dimensions.applicability: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review. Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.

dimensions.label: Conditional juvenile safeguards
dimensions.standard: Proceedings for juveniles must take account of age and the desirability of promoting rehabilitation.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date.
dimensions.exceptions: Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.
questions: What age/status applies at the event date?
What age-appropriate procedure, assistance and rehabilitation/diversion protections were used?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date. Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.

dimensions.label: Conditional protection from double jeopardy
dimensions.standard: No repeated trial or punishment for an offence after final conviction/acquittal under the law and penal procedure of the same country.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence.
dimensions.exceptions: Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. Higher review and narrowly justified resumption on exceptional grounds are distinct; the Covenant does not automatically prohibit prosecutions in different national jurisdictions.
questions: Was a prior decision final, for the same offence in the same country?
Is this a new prosecution or permitted review/resumption, on what grounds?
dimensions.applicability: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence. Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. dimensions.label: Conditional miscarriage-of-justice compensation
dimensions.standard: Compensation according to law where a final conviction is reversed or a pardon granted because a new/newly discovered fact conclusively shows miscarriage of justice, subject to non-disclosure conditions.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction.
dimensions.exceptions: Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.
questions: Do final conviction, punishment, qualifying reversal/pardon and new fact meet the conditions?
What compensation route and non-disclosure exception apply?
dimensions.applicability: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction. Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.

dimensions.label: Notice of charges

dimensions.applicability: Criminal charges; distinguish formal charge notice from arrest reasons under Article 9. Language, detail and timing require case evidence.

dimensions.label: Counsel and preparation

dimensions.applicability: Criminal charges; adequacy depends on complexity, access, timing and circumstances. Assigned counsel is subject to the treaty's conditions.

dimensions.label: Challenge evidence and witnesses

dimensions.applicability: Criminal charges; assess relevant requests, access, refusals and procedural reasons. This does not guarantee unlimited admission of every proposed witness.

dimensions.label: Independent and impartial hearing

dimensions.applicability: Criminal charges and rights/obligations in a suit at law; lawful exceptions to public access require specific assessment. An adverse decision does not establish bias.

dimensions.label: Competent, independent, impartial tribunal established by law
dimensions.standard: The adjudicating tribunal must be competent, independent, impartial and established by law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law.
dimensions.exceptions: An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.
questions: What law establishes the tribunal's authority?
What evidence addresses competence, interference, conflicts or objective appearance of bias?
dimensions.applicability: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law. An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.

dimensions.label: Equality before courts and equality of arms
dimensions.standard: Equality before courts and tribunals requires equal access and procedural opportunities; distinctions require objective, reasonable justification without actual disadvantage or unfairness.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law.
dimensions.exceptions: Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.
questions: Could the parties access the tribunal and make submissions?
Did disclosure, resources or procedure put one party at material disadvantage, with what justification?
dimensions.applicability: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law. Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.

dimensions.label: Public hearings and public judgments
dimensions.standard: Hearings and judgments must ordinarily be public; permitted exclusions and judgment exceptions require case-specific justification.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Hearing and judgment in determination of a criminal charge or suit at law; determine hearing type, as not every pretrial/appeal step requires a public hearing.
dimensions.exceptions: Press/public may be excluded for morals, public order, national security in a democratic society, private lives, or strictly necessary special circumstances where publicity prejudices justice. Judgment exceptions include juvenile interests or matrimonial/child guardianship disputes.
questions: Was the hearing open to the public, and were any exclusions justified?
Was the judgment made public, subject to applicable exceptions?
components: Exception justification; missing web copies are evidence gaps, not proof
dimensions.applicability: Hearing and judgment in determination of a criminal charge or suit at law; determine hearing type, as not every pretrial/appeal step requires a public hearing. Press/public may be excluded for morals, public order, national security in a democratic society, private lives, or strictly necessary special circumstances where publicity prejudices justice. Judgment exceptions include juvenile interests or matrimonial/child guardianship disputes.

dimensions.label: Presumption of innocence
dimensions.standard: Everyone charged with a criminal offence is presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law; the prosecution bears the burden and authorities must refrain from prejudging guilt.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through adjudication.
dimensions.exceptions: Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.
questions: Who bore the burden and what proof standard was used?
Did authorities prejudge guilt or present the accused as guilty?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through adjudication. Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.

dimensions.label: Notice of charges
dimensions.standard: Prompt, detailed notice in a language understood of the nature and cause of the criminal charge.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges.
dimensions.exceptions: Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.
questions: When did the person learn the charge and alleged acts?
What details and language were provided?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges. Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.

dimensions.label: Adequate time and facilities for defence
dimensions.standard: Adequate time and facilities to prepare the defence, including access to relevant documents and other evidence needed for defence.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps.
dimensions.exceptions: Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.
questions: What preparation time, case complexity and disclosure were available?
Were necessary adjournments/access requested and how were requests decided?
dimensions.applicability: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps. Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.

dimensions.label: Access to effective legal assistance
dimensions.standard: Defence in person or through legal assistance of choice, confidential access to counsel, and assigned effective assistance where justice requires subject to means conditions.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal defence; distinguish custodial/investigation guarantees under Article 9 and applicable domestic law.
dimensions.exceptions: Assigned assistance depends on interests of justice and lack of means for free assistance. Self-representation restrictions require objective sufficiently serious reasons; attributed counsel errors require case-specific responsibility analysis.
questions: Was counsel chosen/assigned, accessible and confidential?
Were required assistance and effective representation available, with what restrictions?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal defence; distinguish custodial/investigation guarantees under Article 9 and applicable domestic law. Assigned assistance depends on interests of justice and lack of means for free assistance. Self-representation restrictions require objective sufficiently serious reasons; attributed counsel errors require case-specific responsibility analysis.

dimensions.label: Presence and meaningful participation
dimensions.standard: An accused ordinarily has a right to be tried in their presence and meaningfully defend the case.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal trial and defence participation.
dimensions.exceptions: Proceedings in absence can be permissible in specific circumstances after sufficient notice and opportunity; verify steps informing the accused and justification, not absence alone.
questions: Was the accused present, informed and able to follow/respond?
If absent or restricted, what notice/opportunity and reasons existed?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal trial and defence participation. Proceedings in absence can be permissible in specific circumstances after sufficient notice and opportunity; verify steps informing the accused and justification, not absence alone.

dimensions.label: Examine witnesses and present defence evidence
dimensions.standard: Examine prosecution witnesses and obtain/examine defence witnesses under the same conditions; meaningful opportunity to challenge material evidence.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal trial and material defence evidence requests.
dimensions.exceptions: This is not an unlimited right to call every witness. Identify relevance, requests, refusals, reasons and disadvantage.
questions: Could material prosecution witnesses/evidence be challenged?
Could relevant defence witnesses/evidence be presented under comparable conditions?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal trial and material defence evidence requests. This is not an unlimited right to call every witness. Identify relevance, requests, refusals, reasons and disadvantage.

dimensions.label: Interpretation where required
dimensions.standard: Free assistance of an interpreter where the accused cannot understand or speak the language used in court.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken.
dimensions.exceptions: Nationality or multilingual setting alone does not prove need or adequacy. This right does not require proceedings in the preferred language where the court language is sufficiently understood.
questions: What language ability and proceedings language are documented?
Was free, adequate interpretation provided throughout relevant proceedings?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken. Nationality or multilingual setting alone does not prove need or adequacy. This right does not require proceedings in the preferred language where the court language is sufficiently understood.

dimensions.label: Protection against compelled self-incrimination
dimensions.standard: No compulsion to testify against oneself or confess guilt; exclude prohibited coercion and examine allegations of involuntary statements.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial.
dimensions.exceptions: Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.
questions: How was the statement obtained and was compulsion alleged?
How did the court handle coercion allegations and use/exclusion?
dimensions.applicability: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial. Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.

dimensions.label: Trial without undue delay
dimensions.standard: Criminal proceedings must proceed without undue delay, assessed from formal charge through final judgment including appeal.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal.
dimensions.exceptions: Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.
questions: What intervals, procedural steps and reasons for delay are documented?
How do complexity, party conduct, court conduct and detention affect adequacy?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal. Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.

dimensions.label: Review of conviction and sentence
dimensions.standard: Conviction and sentence must be reviewed by a higher tribunal according to law, including sufficient substantive review of facts and law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review.
dimensions.exceptions: Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.
questions: Was higher review available and effective for both conviction and sentence?
What facts/law, judgment and record were reviewed and what barriers existed?
dimensions.applicability: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review. Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.

dimensions.label: Conditional juvenile safeguards
dimensions.standard: Proceedings for juveniles must take account of age and the desirability of promoting rehabilitation.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date.
dimensions.exceptions: Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.
questions: What age/status applies at the event date?
What age-appropriate procedure, assistance and rehabilitation/diversion protections were used?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date. Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.

The 1987 Constitution supplies judicial authority, including original jurisdiction for certiorari/prohibition. dimensions.explanation: Anchor 0 is confined to the documented access and opportunity-to-present components. JP0036-JP0037 document the initial concern that Chavez was not a broadcaster and had not shown a personal stake; JP0039 records that this obstacle did not prevent adjudication here. dimensions.explanation: Anchor 1: the warnings identify the Anti-Wiretapping Act and program circulars, so this is not a finding that no written legal basis existed. Republic Act 4200 section 1 addresses unlawfully obtained private communications and knowing possession/replay/communication, with conditions and exceptions. dimensions.explanation: Anchor 2: the majority applies the domestic clear-and-present-danger test to content-based restrictions across media, finds respondents’ proof inadequate and nullifies the official warnings. It distinguishes ordinary prosecution of proven law violations from prior restraint and identifies officials’ prosecution/licensing authority as a source of chilling effect. Unauthenticated-tape/false-information concerns, promised due process, continued airing and the NTC/KBP denial are material contrary accounts; the majority explains why absence of a formal order is not decisive. The retained judgment also preserves different treatment for content-neutral regulation (JP0106), so its rule is not converted into a ban on all broadcasting regulation. Article 19(3) necessity supports concern on these facts; GC34’s proportionality/direct-threat language is later interpretation. The Court’s legal conclusion is attributed extraction, not independent HRC adjudication or a measured impact result.

claims.text: Selected judgment passage 115.
claims.excerpt: This is not all the faultline in the stance of the respondents. We slide to the issue of whether the mere press statements of the Secretary of Justice and of the NTC in question constitute a form of content-based prior restraint that has transgressed the Constitution. In resolving this issue, we hold that it is not decisive that the press statements made by respondents were not reduced in or followed up with formal orders or circulars. It is sufficient that the press statements were made by respondents while in the exercise of their official functions. Undoubtedly, respondent Gonzales made his statements as Secretary of Justice, while the NTC issued its statement as the regulatory body of media. Any act done, such as a speech uttered, for and on behalf of the government in an official capacity is covered by the rule on prior restraint. The concept of an "act" does not limit itself to acts already converted to a formal order or official circular. Otherwise, the non formalization of an act into an official order or circular will result in the easy circumvention of the prohibition on prior restraint. The press statements at bar are acts that should be struck down as they constitute impermissible forms of prior restraints on the right to free speech and press.

claims.text: Chavez judgment passage 36: Majority Court reasoning or disposition.
claims.excerpt: To be sure, the circumstances of this case make the constitutional challenge peculiar. Petitioner, who is not a member of the broadcast media, prays that we strike down the acts and statements made by respondents as violations of the right to free speech, free expression and a free press. For another, the recipients of the press statements have not come forward—neither intervening nor joining petitioner in this action. Indeed, as a group, they issued a joint statement with respondent NTC that does not complain about restraints on freedom of the press.
claims.locator: Derived HTML paragraph 36 (not an official paragraph number)
claims.date_note: Date identifies judgment/caption/reasoning, not an inferred date of every underlying fact. Publication date unknown; retrieval 2026-10-10 separate.
claims.attribution: Majority Court reasoning or disposition in Supreme Court of the Philippines majority judgment (2008-02-15), reproduced by LawPhil. Single judgment source; no independent corroboration or source authentication.
claims.verification: Source-attributed candidate claim; not independently verified.

claims.text: Chavez judgment passage 37: Majority Court reasoning or disposition.
claims.excerpt: It would seem, then, that petitioner has not met the requisite legal standing, having failed to allege "such a personal stake in the outcome of the controversy as to assure that concrete adverseness which sharpens the presentation of issues upon which the Court so largely depends for illumination of difficult constitutional questions." 19
claims.locator: Derived HTML paragraph 37 (not an official paragraph number)
claims.date_note: Date identifies judgment/caption/reasoning, not an inferred date of every underlying fact. Publication date unknown; retrieval 2026-10-10 separate.
claims.attribution: Majority Court reasoning or disposition in Supreme Court of the Philippines majority judgment (2008-02-15), reproduced by LawPhil. Single judgment source; no independent corroboration or source authentication.
claims.verification: Source-attributed candidate claim; not independently verified.

claims.text: Chavez judgment passage 38: Majority Court reasoning or disposition.
claims.excerpt: But as early as half a century ago, we have already held that where serious constitutional questions are involved, "the transcendental importance to the public of these cases demands that they be settled promptly and definitely, brushing aside if we must, technicalities of procedure." 20 Subsequently, this Court has repeatedly and consistently refused to wield procedural barriers as impediments to its addressing and resolving serious legal questions that greatly impact on public interest,21 in keeping with the Court's duty under the 1987 Constitution to determine whether or not other branches of government have kept themselves within the limits of the Constitution and the laws and that they have not abused the discretion given to them.
claims.locator: Derived HTML paragraph 38 (not an official paragraph number)
claims.date_note: Date identifies judgment/caption/reasoning, not an inferred date of every underlying fact. Publication date unknown; retrieval 2026-10-10 separate.
claims.attribution: Majority Court reasoning or disposition in Supreme Court of the Philippines majority judgment (2008-02-15), reproduced by LawPhil. Single judgment source; no independent corroboration or source authentication.
claims.verification: Source-attributed candidate claim; not independently verified.

claims.text: Chavez judgment passage 39: Majority Court reasoning or disposition.
claims.excerpt: Thus, in line with the liberal policy of this Court on locus standi when a case involves an issue of overarching significance to our society,22 we therefore brush aside technicalities of procedure and take cognizance of this petition,23 seeing as it involves a challenge to the most exalted of all the civil rights, the freedom of expression. The petition raises other issues like the extent of the right to information of the public. It is fundamental, however, that we need not address all issues but only the most decisive one which in the case at bar is whether the acts of the respondents abridge freedom of speech and of the press.
claims.locator: Derived HTML paragraph 39 (not an official paragraph number)
claims.date_note: Date identifies judgment/caption/reasoning, not an inferred date of every underlying fact. Publication date unknown; retrieval 2026-10-10 separate.
claims.attribution: Majority Court reasoning or disposition in Supreme Court of the Philippines majority judgment (2008-02-15), reproduced by LawPhil. Single judgment source; no independent corroboration or source authentication.

claims.text: Chavez judgment passage 75: Majority Court reasoning or disposition.
claims.excerpt: With respect to content-based restrictions, the government must also show the type of harm the speech sought to be restrained would bring about— especially the gravity and the imminence of the threatened harm – otherwise the prior restraint will be invalid. Prior restraint on speech based on its content cannot be justified by hypothetical fears, "but only by showing a substantive and imminent evil that has taken the life of a reality already on ground."67 As formulated, "the question in every case is whether the words used are used in such circumstances and are of such a nature as to create a clear and present danger that they will bring about the substantive evils that Congress has a right to prevent. It is a question of proximity and degree."68
claims.locator: Derived HTML paragraph 75 (not an official paragraph number)
claims.date_note: Date identifies judgment/caption/reasoning, not an inferred date of every underlying fact. Publication date unknown; retrieval 2026-10-10 separate.
claims.attribution: Majority Court reasoning or disposition in Supreme Court of the Philippines majority judgment (2008-02-15), reproduced by LawPhil. Single judgment source; no independent corroboration or source authentication.

claims.text: Chavez judgment passage 77: Majority Court reasoning or disposition.
claims.excerpt: Also, the incidental restriction on speech must be no greater than what is essential to the furtherance of that interest. 70 A restriction that is so broad that it encompasses more than what is required to satisfy the governmental interest will be invalidated. 71 The regulation, therefore, must be reasonable and narrowly drawn to fit the regulatory purpose, with the least restrictive means undertaken. 72
claims.locator: Derived HTML paragraph 77 (not an official paragraph number)

claims.text: Chavez judgment passage 79: Majority Court reasoning or disposition.
claims.excerpt: Applying the foregoing, it is clear that the challenged acts in the case at bar need to be subjected to the clear and present danger rule, as they are content-based restrictions. The acts of respondents focused solely on but one object—a specific content— fixed as these were on the alleged taped conversations between the President and a COMELEC official. Undoubtedly these did not merely provide regulations as to the time, place or manner of the dissemination of speech or expression.
claims.locator: Derived HTML paragraph 79 (not an official paragraph number)
claims.date_note: Date identifies judgment/caption/reasoning, not an inferred date of every underlying fact. Publication date unknown; retrieval 2026-10-10 separate.
claims.attribution: Majority Court reasoning or disposition in Supreme Court of the Philippines majority judgment (2008-02-15), reproduced by LawPhil. Single judgment source; no independent corroboration or source authentication.
claims.verification: Source-attributed candidate claim; not independently verified.

claims.text: Chavez judgment passage 106: Majority Court reasoning or disposition.
claims.excerpt: This is not to suggest, however, that the clear and present danger rule has been applied to all cases that involve the broadcast media. The rule applies to all media, including broadcast, but only when the challenged act is a content-based regulation that infringes on free speech, expression and the press. Indeed, in Osmena v. COMELEC,90 which also involved broadcast media, the Court refused to apply the clear and present danger rule to a COMELEC regulation of time and manner of advertising of political advertisements because the challenged restriction was content-neutral.91 And in a case involving due process and equal protection issues, the Court in Telecommunications and Broadcast Attorneys of the Philippines v. COMELEC92 treated a restriction imposed on a broadcast media as a reasonable condition for the grant of the media’s franchise, without going into which test would apply.
claims.locator: Derived HTML paragraph 106 (not an official paragraph number)

claims.verification: Source-attributed candidate claim; not independently verified.

claims.text: Chavez judgment passage 112: Majority Court reasoning or disposition.
claims.excerpt: Having settled the applicable standard to content-based restrictions on broadcast media, let us go to its application to the case at bar. To recapitulate, a governmental action that restricts freedom of speech or of the press based on content is given the strictest scrutiny, with the government having the burden of overcoming the presumed unconstitutionality by the clear and present danger rule. This rule applies equally to all kinds of media, including broadcast media.
claims.locator: Derived HTML paragraph 112 (not an official paragraph number)
claims.date_note: Date identifies judgment/caption/reasoning, not an inferred date of every underlying fact. Publication date unknown; retrieval 2026-10-10 separate.

claims.text: Chavez judgment passage 113: Majority Court reasoning or disposition.
claims.excerpt: This outlines the procedural map to follow in cases like the one at bar as it spells out the following: (a) the test; (b) the presumption; (c) the burden of proof; (d) the party to discharge the burden; and (e) the quantum of evidence necessary. On the basis of the records of the case at bar, respondents who have the burden to show that these acts do not abridge freedom of speech and of the press failed to hurdle the clear and present danger test. It appears that the great evil which government wants to prevent is the airing of a tape recording in alleged violation of the anti-wiretapping law. The records of the case at bar, however, are confused and confusing, and respondents’ evidence falls short of satisfying the clear and present danger test. Firstly, the various statements of the Press Secretary obfuscate the identity of the voices in the tape recording. Secondly, the integrity of the taped conversation is also suspect. The Press Secretary showed to the public two versions, one supposed to be a "complete" version and the other, an "altered" version. Thirdly, the evidence of the respondents on the who’s and the how’s of the wiretapping act is ambivalent, especially considering the tape’s different versions. The identity of the wire-tappers, the manner of its commission and other related and relevant proofs are some of the invisibles of this case. Fourthly, given all these unsettled facets of the tape, it is even arguable whether its airing would violate the anti-wiretapping law.

claims.text: Chavez judgment passage 114: Majority Court reasoning or disposition.
claims.excerpt: We rule that not every violation of a law will justify straitjacketing the exercise of freedom of speech and of the press. Our laws are of different kinds and doubtless, some of them provide norms of conduct which even if violated have only an adverse effect on a person’s private comfort but does not endanger national security. There are laws of great significance but their violation, by itself and without more, cannot support suppression of free speech and free press. In fine, violation of law is just a factor, a vital one to be sure, which should be weighed in adjudging whether to restrain freedom of speech and of the press. The totality of the injurious effects of the violation to private and public interest must be calibrated in light of the preferred status accorded by the Constitution and by related international covenants protecting freedom of speech and of the press. In calling for a careful and calibrated measurement of the circumference of all these factors to determine compliance with the clear and present danger test, the Court should not be misinterpreted as devaluing violations of law. By all means, violations of law should be vigorously prosecuted by the State for they breed their own evil consequence. But to repeat, the need to prevent their violation cannot per se trump the exercise of free speech and free press, a preferred right whose breach can lead to greater evils. For this failure of the respondents alone to offer proof to satisfy the clear and present danger test, the Court has no option but to uphold the exercise of free speech and free press. There is no showing that the feared violation of the anti-wiretapping law clearly endangers the national security of the State.
claims.locator: Derived HTML paragraph 114 (not an official paragraph number)

claims.text: Chavez judgment passage 116: Majority Court reasoning or disposition.
claims.excerpt: There is enough evidence of chilling effect of the complained acts on record. The warnings given to media came from no less the NTC, a regulatory agency that can cancel the Certificate of Authority of the radio and broadcast media. They also came from the Secretary of Justice, the alter ego of the Executive, who wields the awesome power to prosecute those perceived to be violating the laws of the land. After the warnings, the KBP inexplicably joined the NTC in issuing an ambivalent Joint Press Statement. After the warnings, petitioner Chavez was left alone to fight this battle for freedom of speech and of the press. This silence on the sidelines on the part of some media practitioners is too deafening to be the subject of misinterpretation.

dimensions.label: Competent, independent, impartial tribunal established by law
dimensions.standard: The adjudicating tribunal must be competent, independent, impartial and established by law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law.
dimensions.exceptions: An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.
questions: What law establishes the tribunal's authority?
What evidence addresses competence, interference, conflicts or objective appearance of bias?
dimensions.applicability: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law. An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.

dimensions.label: Equality before courts and equality of arms
dimensions.standard: Equality before courts and tribunals requires equal access and procedural opportunities; distinctions require objective, reasonable justification without actual disadvantage or unfairness.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law.
dimensions.exceptions: Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.
questions: Could the parties access the tribunal and make submissions?
Did disclosure, resources or procedure put one party at material disadvantage, with what justification?
dimensions.applicability: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law. Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.

dimensions.label: Public hearings and public judgments
dimensions.standard: Hearings and judgments must ordinarily be public; permitted exclusions and judgment exceptions require case-specific justification.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Hearing and judgment in determination of a criminal charge or suit at law; determine hearing type, as not every pretrial/appeal step requires a public hearing.
dimensions.exceptions: Press/public may be excluded for morals, public order, national security in a democratic society, private lives, or strictly necessary special circumstances where publicity prejudices justice. Judgment exceptions include juvenile interests or matrimonial/child guardianship disputes.
questions: Was the hearing open to the public, and were any exclusions justified?
Was the judgment made public, subject to applicable exceptions?
components: Exception justification; missing web copies are evidence gaps, not proof
dimensions.applicability: Hearing and judgment in determination of a criminal charge or suit at law; determine hearing type, as not every pretrial/appeal step requires a public hearing. Press/public may be excluded for morals, public order, national security in a democratic society, private lives, or strictly necessary special circumstances where publicity prejudices justice. Judgment exceptions include juvenile interests or matrimonial/child guardianship disputes.

dimensions.label: Presumption of innocence
dimensions.standard: Everyone charged with a criminal offence is presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law; the prosecution bears the burden and authorities must refrain from prejudging guilt.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through adjudication.
dimensions.exceptions: Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.
questions: Who bore the burden and what proof standard was used?
Did authorities prejudge guilt or present the accused as guilty?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through adjudication. Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.

dimensions.label: Notice of charges
dimensions.standard: Prompt, detailed notice in a language understood of the nature and cause of the criminal charge.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges.
dimensions.exceptions: Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.
questions: When did the person learn the charge and alleged acts?
What details and language were provided?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges. Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.

dimensions.label: Adequate time and facilities for defence
dimensions.standard: Adequate time and facilities to prepare the defence, including access to relevant documents and other evidence needed for defence.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps.
dimensions.exceptions: Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.
questions: What preparation time, case complexity and disclosure were available?
Were necessary adjournments/access requested and how were requests decided?
dimensions.applicability: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps. Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.

dimensions.label: Access to effective legal assistance
dimensions.standard: Defence in person or through legal assistance of choice, confidential access to counsel, and assigned effective assistance where justice requires subject to means conditions.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal defence; distinguish custodial/investigation guarantees under Article 9 and applicable domestic law.
dimensions.exceptions: Assigned assistance depends on interests of justice and lack of means for free assistance. Self-representation restrictions require objective sufficiently serious reasons; attributed counsel errors require case-specific responsibility analysis.
questions: Was counsel chosen/assigned, accessible and confidential?
Were required assistance and effective representation available, with what restrictions?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal defence; distinguish custodial/investigation guarantees under Article 9 and applicable domestic law. Assigned assistance depends on interests of justice and lack of means for free assistance. Self-representation restrictions require objective sufficiently serious reasons; attributed counsel errors require case-specific responsibility analysis.

dimensions.label: Presence and meaningful participation
dimensions.standard: An accused ordinarily has a right to be tried in their presence and meaningfully defend the case.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal trial and defence participation.
dimensions.exceptions: Proceedings in absence can be permissible in specific circumstances after sufficient notice and opportunity; verify steps informing the accused and justification, not absence alone.
questions: Was the accused present, informed and able to follow/respond?
If absent or restricted, what notice/opportunity and reasons existed?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal trial and defence participation. Proceedings in absence can be permissible in specific circumstances after sufficient notice and opportunity; verify steps informing the accused and justification, not absence alone.

dimensions.label: Examine witnesses and present defence evidence
dimensions.standard: Examine prosecution witnesses and obtain/examine defence witnesses under the same conditions; meaningful opportunity to challenge material evidence.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal trial and material defence evidence requests.
dimensions.exceptions: This is not an unlimited right to call every witness. Identify relevance, requests, refusals, reasons and disadvantage.
questions: Could material prosecution witnesses/evidence be challenged?
Could relevant defence witnesses/evidence be presented under comparable conditions?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal trial and material defence evidence requests. This is not an unlimited right to call every witness. Identify relevance, requests, refusals, reasons and disadvantage.

dimensions.label: Interpretation where required
dimensions.standard: Free assistance of an interpreter where the accused cannot understand or speak the language used in court.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken.
dimensions.exceptions: Nationality or multilingual setting alone does not prove need or adequacy. This right does not require proceedings in the preferred language where the court language is sufficiently understood.
questions: What language ability and proceedings language are documented?
Was free, adequate interpretation provided throughout relevant proceedings?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken. Nationality or multilingual setting alone does not prove need or adequacy. This right does not require proceedings in the preferred language where the court language is sufficiently understood.

dimensions.label: Protection against compelled self-incrimination
dimensions.standard: No compulsion to testify against oneself or confess guilt; exclude prohibited coercion and examine allegations of involuntary statements.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial.
dimensions.exceptions: Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.
questions: How was the statement obtained and was compulsion alleged?
How did the court handle coercion allegations and use/exclusion?
dimensions.applicability: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial. Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.

dimensions.label: Trial without undue delay
dimensions.standard: Criminal proceedings must proceed without undue delay, assessed from formal charge through final judgment including appeal.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal.
dimensions.exceptions: Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.
questions: What intervals, procedural steps and reasons for delay are documented?
How do complexity, party conduct, court conduct and detention affect adequacy?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal. Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.

dimensions.label: Review of conviction and sentence
dimensions.standard: Conviction and sentence must be reviewed by a higher tribunal according to law, including sufficient substantive review of facts and law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review.
dimensions.exceptions: Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.
questions: Was higher review available and effective for both conviction and sentence?
What facts/law, judgment and record were reviewed and what barriers existed?
dimensions.applicability: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review. Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.

dimensions.label: Conditional juvenile safeguards
dimensions.standard: Proceedings for juveniles must take account of age and the desirability of promoting rehabilitation.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date.
dimensions.exceptions: Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.
questions: What age/status applies at the event date?
What age-appropriate procedure, assistance and rehabilitation/diversion protections were used?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date. Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.

dimensions.label: Conditional protection from double jeopardy
dimensions.standard: No repeated trial or punishment for an offence after final conviction/acquittal under the law and penal procedure of the same country.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence.
dimensions.exceptions: Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. Higher review and narrowly justified resumption on exceptional grounds are distinct; the Covenant does not automatically prohibit prosecutions in different national jurisdictions.
questions: Was a prior decision final, for the same offence in the same country?
Is this a new prosecution or permitted review/resumption, on what grounds?
dimensions.applicability: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence. Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. Higher review and narrowly justified resumption on exceptional grounds are distinct; the Covenant does not automatically prohibit prosecutions in different national jurisdictions.

dimensions.label: Conditional miscarriage-of-justice compensation
dimensions.standard: Compensation according to law where a final conviction is reversed or a pardon granted because a new/newly discovered fact conclusively shows miscarriage of justice, subject to non-disclosure conditions.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction.
dimensions.exceptions: Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.
questions: Do final conviction, punishment, qualifying reversal/pardon and new fact meet the conditions?
What compensation route and non-disclosure exception apply?
dimensions.applicability: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction. Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.

dimensions.label: Expression and restrictive interference
dimensions.standard: Identify the expression, whether Article 19 protects it and the specific restriction. Freedom to hold opinions without interference is distinct from expression restrictions.
dimensions.applicability: Do not presume expression was involved in every prosecution. Identify conduct and restriction; Article 20 duties and other rights may also require analysis.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR Article 19 and relevant domestic law at the event date.
dimensions.stage: Identified expression and interference/restriction, including prosecution where linked.
dimensions.exceptions: Do not presume expression was involved in every prosecution. Identify conduct and restriction; Article 20 duties and other rights may also require analysis.
questions: What expression, restriction, law, asserted aim and particular justification are documented?
What competing account or missing facts would change this dimension's assessment?

dimensions.label: Restriction's legal basis
dimensions.standard: Any restriction of protected expression must be provided by law with sufficient precision and accessible guidance; discretion must be bounded.
dimensions.applicability: First establish expression and restriction. Citation of a statute alone does not settle foreseeability or its application.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR Article 19 and relevant domestic law at the event date.
dimensions.stage: Identified expression and interference/restriction, including prosecution where linked.
dimensions.exceptions: First establish expression and restriction. Citation of a statute alone does not settle foreseeability or its application.
questions: What expression, restriction, law, asserted aim and particular justification are documented?

dimensions.label: Asserted legitimate aim
dimensions.standard: Expression restrictions must serve the rights or reputations of others, national security, public order, public health or morals; asserted reasons require attribution and scrutiny.
dimensions.applicability: An asserted aim is a government position, not proof of necessity or legitimacy in the particular application. Missing government reasons remain unknown.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR Article 19 and relevant domestic law at the event date.
dimensions.stage: Identified expression and interference/restriction, including prosecution where linked.
dimensions.exceptions: An asserted aim is a government position, not proof of necessity or legitimacy in the particular application. Missing government reasons remain unknown.
questions: What expression, restriction, law, asserted aim and particular justification are documented?
What competing account or missing facts would change this dimension's assessment?

dimensions.label: Necessity and proportionality
dimensions.standard: A restriction must be necessary and proportionate to a permitted aim, with a specific direct connection between the expression and the threat; examine less intrusive measures.
dimensions.applicability: Assess actual expression, aim, harm, penalty and alternatives. A restriction is not automatically unlawful; a legal basis and aim do not automatically establish necessity.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR Article 19 and relevant domestic law at the event date.
dimensions.stage: Identified expression and interference/restriction, including prosecution where linked.
dimensions.exceptions: Assess actual expression, aim, harm, penalty and alternatives. A restriction is not automatically unlawful; a legal basis and aim do not automatically establish necessity.

What competing account or missing facts would change this dimension's assessment?

rubric.scoring_method: Analyst selects an anchored concern level and supplies supported propositions and reasoning. The server maps its name to 0–3, validates references and snapshots evidence. It does not infer legal facts or automatically select severity.
rubric.confidence_method: Analyst judgment of reliability and support for this dimension, separately recorded. Distinct reports are not automatically independent corroboration.
rubric.completeness_method: Analyst judgment of relevant factual/legal coverage for this dimension; missing information is unknown.
rubric.limits: No combined percentage, calibrated probability, official TrialWatch grade or definitive violation finding. Country indicators cannot change individual scores. This is a partial rubric, not an exhaustive legal checklist.

expression.explanation: Anchor 2: the judgment records threats of criminal liability/arrest, investigation of media and licence suspension/revocation tied to airing a specific politically significant recording. The Court characterises the acts as content-based prior restraint and finds chilling effect. JP0024-JP0025 reproduce the NTC/KBP denial of censorship and JP0034 reports continued airing; these limit claims about practical suppression but do not erase the documented official threats. The score concerns the June 2005 interference described by the Court, not the existence of an ongoing restriction after the 2008 remedy. No conviction, imprisonment, licence cancellation or measured audience loss is established, so severe/3 is not assigned.
expression.next_verification: Review the quoted warnings and contrary joint statement with the majority reasoning; keep actual implementation and separate-opinion questions unresolved.
expression.applicability: ICCPR Article 19(2), and Constitution Article III section 4, apply to media dissemination and public political information. June 2005 interference, assessed retrospectively through the 2008 majority record. GC34 paragraphs 11-13 are labelled later 2011 interpretation, not event-time law.

missing_facts: Full event-time text and enabling authority for the cited NTC circulars; the warning quotes are not the complete circulars.
Authenticity, unlawful acquisition, knowledge and relevant statutory exceptions in the concrete tape circumstances.
Separate-opinion interpretation and precise boundaries of executive authority are unexamined.
expression.explanation: Anchor 1: the warnings identify the Anti-Wiretapping Act and program circulars, so this is not a finding that no written legal basis existed. Republic Act 4200 section 1 addresses unlawfully obtained private communications and knowing possession/replay/communication, with conditions and exceptions. The Court finds the identity, integrity and acquisition circumstances of the tape unsettled and even whether airing violated the law arguable (JP0113). Applying an automatic continuing-offence/licence-warning premise before those predicates were established raises a specific legal-application concern. The Court’s statement that violations may be prosecuted (JP0114), promised process (JP0022) and respondents’ regulatory argument (JP0034) remain visible. This analysis does not declare RA4200 facially vague, invalid, or inapplicable in every situation.
expression.next_verification: Have a Philippine-law reviewer match RA4200’s elements/exceptions and NTC authority to the warning text without treating the Court’s expression remedy as blanket immunity from criminal law.
expression.applicability: Article 19(3) law condition and 1987 Constitution expression/privacy provisions at June 2005. GC34 paragraphs 24-25 supply a distinctly later 2011 precision/discretion framework; the pending score primarily concerns documented application uncertainty, not a retroactive facial-law conclusion.

missing_facts: Specific right-holder/privacy interest and direct harm asserted for this recording.
Precise public-order/national-security threat evidence and why the particular restriction addressed it.
Underlying respondents’ pleadings and separate opinions.
expression.explanation: Anchor 1: the reproduced NTC warning invokes the unusual national situation, unauthenticated/false recordings and prevention of illegal wiretapping or incitement. Protection of private communication and genuine public-order/national-security interests can be relevant Article 19(3) aims. However, preventing a statutory violation alone does not establish which permitted aim is served by this particular restriction. The Court found no showing that the feared law violation clearly endangered national security; the exact privacy injury and threatened harm were not resolved. The NTC/KBP verification and non-incitement statements are competing protective rationales, not proof of necessity. Concern is limited because this record does not establish that every asserted purpose was impermissible or a pretext.
expression.next_verification: Separate each asserted purpose from the Court’s evidentiary findings, and identify the concrete protected interest before moving to necessity.
expression.applicability: Article 19(3)(a)-(b) and Constitution Article III sections 3-4 at the June 2005 events. Later GC34 paragraphs 21-23 and 28-32 assist the modern retrospective worksheet and are not treated as standards published in 2005/2008.

No later compliance, finality/reconsideration or current-status record is supplied.
expression.explanation: Anchor 2: the majority applies the domestic clear-and-present-danger test to content-based restrictions across media, finds respondents’ proof inadequate and nullifies the official warnings. It distinguishes ordinary prosecution of proven law violations from prior restraint and identifies officials’ prosecution/licensing authority as a source of chilling effect. Unauthenticated-tape/false-information concerns, promised due process, continued airing and the NTC/KBP denial are material contrary accounts; the majority explains why absence of a formal order is not decisive. The retained judgment also preserves different treatment for content-neutral regulation (JP0106), so its rule is not converted into a ban on all broadcasting regulation. Article 19(3) necessity supports concern on these facts; GC34’s proportionality/direct-threat language is later interpretation. The Court’s legal conclusion is attributed extraction, not independent HRC adjudication or a measured impact result.
expression.next_verification: Review whether narrower targeted investigation or correction/verification could address asserted harms; examine separate opinions only under a separately authorised document step. Retain the historical Court remedy and contrary record without inferring present effects.

GC34 paragraphs 22 and 33-35 (2011) are later explanatory guidance; no numerical probability or automatic legal finding follows.

claims.text: Chavez judgment passage 75: Majority Court reasoning or disposition.
claims.excerpt: With respect to content-based restrictions, the government must also show the type of harm the speech sought to be restrained would bring about— especially the gravity and the imminence of the threatened harm – otherwise the prior restraint will be invalid. Prior restraint on speech based on its content cannot be justified by hypothetical fears, "but only by showing a substantive and imminent evil that has taken the life of a reality already on ground."67 As formulated, "the question in every case is whether the words used are used in such circumstances and are of such a nature as to create a clear and present danger that they will bring about the substantive evils that Congress has a right to prevent. It is a question of proximity and degree."68

claims.excerpt: Also, the incidental restriction on speech must be no greater than what is essential to the furtherance of that interest. 70 A restriction that is so broad that it encompasses more than what is required to satisfy the governmental interest will be invalidated. 71 The regulation, therefore, must be reasonable and narrowly drawn to fit the regulatory purpose, with the least restrictive means undertaken. 72
